submission:
Root cause: Not established. The three dispatches that could have observed the failing behaviour — metrics, logs and traces on frontend — all failed at the transport layer with DNS name-resolution failures against observe-namespace endpoints [tr_d5f3b92daf38][tr_d2c58a0eb4fe][tr_3c06a8fe0871], so no error rate, log line or span exists for any service in this incident. The only substantive evidence returned is change history, and it says the same thing for frontend, product-catalog and cart: exactly two records each in the full 24h window, a service-config creation followed one second later by a first-ever workload container creation, all by platform-automation at 22:33:29-30, roughly eight minutes before the 22:41:59 alert [tr_e6c32894b1ee][tr_d3ea444602d8][tr_d9359c8237e6]. That is a scripted stand-up of the whole environment, not a deploy, config edit or flag flip on anything already running. What remains is an alert on a freshly bootstrapped frontend with zero telemetry behind it; naming a mechanism would be inventing one. The one mechanism the evidence does establish is that cluster-internal name resolution for observe.svc.cluster.local is broken from the probing environment, confirmed against three distinct hostnames and ports — that must be fixed before any further dispatch returns anything.

Fault type: unknown

Reasoning:
Each fault class in this taxonomy is identified by a signal from the culprit's own metrics, logs or traces, and none of those were retrieved. The specialists were explicit that the empty results are transport failures, not successful empty queries, and correctly refused to read them as exculpatory for frontend or as evidence of a traffic outage [tr_d5f3b92daf38][tr_d2c58a0eb4fe][tr_3c06a8fe0871]. The change dispatches are high-confidence but only eliminate: no frontend code deploy or image rollout, no flag flip or runtime config edit on a running service, no earlier slow-burn change, no human actor [tr_e6c32894b1ee][tr_d3ea444602d8][tr_d9359c8237e6]. Every record is a first creation, so there is no prior running state for a change to have regressed from — which is why bad_deploy, bad_config and feature_flag all sit poorly. I name frontend only because it is where the alert fired and where blast radius starts, not because evidence places fault there; seven edges were crossed unmeasured and five downstreams were never examined [tr_e6c32894b1ee]. Remediation is 'none' because prescribing a fix for an unidentified mechanism is guessing; the real next action is repairing the observability query path and re-running metrics, logs and traces.

Alternatives considered:
1. frontend: Cluster DNS or network connectivity is broken for the environment stood up at 22:33, so frontend cannot reach its downstreams for the same reason the probes cannot reach Prometheus, Loki and Jaeger. (network_partition). Ranked lower because: All three confirmed resolution failures are against observe-namespace hosts from the probing environment; a partition is diagnosed from the culprit's own log complaining it cannot reach anything, and no frontend log was retrieved [tr_d2c58a0eb4fe].
2. frontend: The 22:33:29 bootstrap created frontend before its downstreams were ready, and frontend failed on first-run dependency discovery against cold or absent backends. (dependency_latency). Ranked lower because: This rests solely on the eight-minute gap between creation records and onset [tr_e6c32894b1ee][tr_d3ea444602d8]; no trace or metric shows any downstream being slow, and the trace specialist explicitly declined to name a guilty downstream [tr_3c06a8fe0871].

Open questions:
- What did frontend actually emit around 22:41:59 — error text, a named downstream, a timeout, or silence? This alone separates freeze, partition, exhaustion and dependency latency, and no log line was retrieved.
- Is the observe-namespace DNS failure confined to the probing environment, or is cluster DNS broken for astronomy-shop workloads too — in which case it may be the incident rather than an obstruction? Possibly the observe namespace was simply never stood up by the same 22:33 bootstrap.
- What is the state of the five unexamined services in the blast radius (ad, checkout, recommendation and others), and did frontend ever serve a successful request after its 22:33:31 container creation?
